subject: Service entitlement review: recurring tail-latency spikes impacting inference
content:
From: Carl Hsu <carl.hsu@fintegral.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@fintegral.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repeated tail-latency spikes affecting nightly inference jobs

Hi Jordan,

We’ve been tracking a pattern of tail-latency spikes over the past three weeks that are impacting our nightly batch scoring pipeline. Most requests are OK, but every ~6–8 hours we see a cluster of 500–800ms tails that cause downstream retries in our orchestrator and occasionally push jobs past SLA windows. I’ve attached a short CSV with sample traces and timestamps.

We’re in renewal conversations and need to understand two things:
- Whether Redwood can provide a short-term entitlement (credit or SLO adjustment) for observed disruptions.
- The practical path to a premium SLA (90ms median / 99.9th percentile target) — what it would take operationally and commercially to move Fintegral onto that tier.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to review the traces and a remediation plan?

Thanks,
Carl
Director, Platform Engineering
Fintegral

Attachment: latency_report_May2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)

----
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: Carl Hsu <carl.hsu@fintegral.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repeated tail-latency spikes affecting nightly inference jobs

Carl — thanks for the detailed note and the traces. I looped in Marissa (account lead) and Evelyn (CS) so we can coordinate the commercial and operational next steps.

Quick summary of what we’ll bring to the call:
- A short RCA plan (data collection + KV-cache/eviction hypothesis)
- Proposal for a 4-week dedicated pilot (observability + targeted scheduling windows) to validate fixes
- Options for an interim credit or one-time goodwill for the impacted windows while we run the pilot

Are you available Wed 20 May 09:00–10:00 PT or Thu 21 May 14:00–15:00 PT?

—Jordan
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

----
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Carl Hsu <carl.hsu@fintegral.com>, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repeated tail-latency spikes affecting nightly inference jobs

Carl, Jordan — thanks for looping me in. I want to be pragmatic about commercial remedies while we work the operational side. A few things from my side:

1) Interim remedy: We can offer a one-time invoice credit equivalent to two days of token usage applied to May billing, conditional on starting the pilot within 10 business days. This is intended to bridge the gap while we validate mitigation.

2) Premium SLA path:
- Dedicated pilot (4 weeks) + shared runbook: verifies tail behavior under your production mix
- If pilot hits agreed thresholds, we’ll present an SLA addendum with 99.9th percentile targets and a pricing delta (typically a fixed percent uplift tied to dedicated capacity and reserved throughput)

3) Risk & data needs: To scope the pilot we need: sample request distribution, sequence-length histogram, and the attached latency CSV is helpful. Please also share your retry logic (thresholds/timeouts).

I can join the call proposed by Jordan on Wed 20 May at 09:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----
From: Carl Hsu <carl.hsu@fintegral.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@fintegral.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repeated tail-latency spikes affecting nightly inference jobs

Thanks — Wed 09:00 PT works. We’ll bring our SRE and the retry logs. A couple of clarifications before the call:
- The spikes tend to cluster around autoscaler events and a handful of long-context requests (>=2k tokens) that coincide with large KV-cache churn. Is dedicated capacity the only way to reduce variance, or can you achieve comparable tail improvements with different batching/quantization profiles?
- For the credit: we prefer a transparent line-item so we can justify to finance — a one-time credit applied to May invoice is fine if you can provide a short note we can attach to procurement.

I’ll add Fintegral SRE (eng@fintegral.com) to the dial.

Carl

----
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: Carl Hsu <carl.hsu@fintegral.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Repeated tail-latency spikes affecting nightly inference jobs

Carl — thanks again for the sync last week. Per our action items, we executed a focused baseline run and validated the KV-cache eviction hypothesis against your provided traces. Summary and proposed path:

Summary findings:
- Verified intermittent KV-cache thrashing correlated with large-context requests during autoscaler smoothing windows.
- Most spikes are not due to quantization; they are primarily queuing variance under bursty moments in the autoscaler.

Proposed remediation & commercial path:
1) Immediate: apply a one-time credit of USD 28,400 to the May invoice (line item: "Service remediation credit — May 2026"). We’ll provide a short note you can attach to procurement.
2) Pilot: 4-week dedicated pilot on a small reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent) with workload-aware autoscale smoothing + prefix cache tuning. Objective: demonstrate 99.9th percentile reduction to <350ms for your nightly batch window.
3) If pilot succeeds: offer an SLA addendum with premium commitments (99.9th percentile target TBD in the addendum) and a commercial uplift of 18% on base usage for dedicated capacity. Addendum draft attached.

Attachments: SLA_addendum_draft.pdf (PDF, 160KB) and the internal run log (latency_report_May2026.csv).

Next steps:
- Confirm pilot start date this week (we can start 27 May).
- Carl: please send the retry logic snippet and sequence-length histogram by EOD Wed 27 May.
- Marissa: I’ll coordinate onboarding and scheduling with infra.

If you want a different commercial structure (e.g., a longer-term reserved commit in exchange for lower uplift), we can model that in the addendum.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: SLA_addendum_draft.pdf (PDF, 160KB), latency_report_May2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)
